ch_phone_note: Needs a SIP account from a carrier
ch_web_note: A bubble on your own site — no account anywhere
ch_telegram_note: Needs a bot token — two minutes to make
ch_email_note: Reads a shared mailbox you already have
ch_messenger_note: Needs a Meta app and page review
ch_signal_note: Runs fully on this machine — no business account
ch_discord_note: Rarely useful for a business; common for clubs
ch_matrix_note: Only if you already run a homeserver
stt_local_body: Good German, including Austrian accents. Nothing leaves the building. This is what the business line was tested on.
stt_deepgram_body: The fastest of the cloud ones and the best at people talking over each other. Audio is sent to them.
stt_azure_body: EU regions available, which some businesses need on paper. Audio is sent to Microsoft.
stt_google_body: Strong on rare words and place names. Audio is sent to Google.
stt_eleven_body: Same account as their voices, so one key and one bill. Slower than Deepgram and dearer than Azure.
stt_openai_body: The same model you could run locally, run by them. Only worth paying for if this machine has no room for it.
stt_cartesia_body: Fast, and pairs with their voices on one key. Newer than the others, so less proven on Austrian German.
stt_custom_body: Whisper.cpp, faster-whisper, VoiceBox, anything with an OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint. Give it a URL and a port.
tts_local_body: Four Austrian and German voices. Plainly synthetic, but instant and free — and callers stop noticing after one sentence.
tts_eleven_body: The most human of the lot. Costs per character and adds a pause before every sentence the agent speaks.
tts_azure_body: Solid German voices, EU hosting, priced far below ElevenLabs.
tts_cartesia_body: Nearly as natural as ElevenLabs and noticeably quicker to start speaking.
tts_deepgram_body: The quickest to start speaking of anything here. Fewer German voices than Azure, and none with an Austrian accent.
tts_google_body: The widest choice of German voices, including Austrian. Priced per character like the rest.
tts_openai_body: Pleasant voices, but the German has an American accent that customers notice.
tts_custom_body: Piper, Kokoro, VoiceBox, XTTS — anything on your network that returns audio. Give it a URL and a port.
trade_empty_note: Nothing is created. Build the catalogue yourself.
seed_clinic_rule2: Outside opening hours the assistant answers
seed_clinic_prompt: You answer the phone for Wagner & Partner. Book, move and confirm appointments from the catalogue. Never promise an outcome and never comment on anything clinical — offer the next free appointment or put the caller through to reception.
seed_trades_rule1: Emergency numbers ring a person day and night
seed_trades_rule2: Unknown numbers go to the assistant
seed_trades_prompt: You answer the phone for Wagner & Partner. Take job details — address, what is broken, when someone can be there — and offer a call-out slot from the catalogue. Never quote a price; a person confirms every price.
seed_restaurant_rule1: Calls during service hours ring the pass
seed_restaurant_rule2: Group bookings always reach a person
seed_restaurant_prompt: You answer the phone for Wagner & Partner. Take table bookings from the catalogue: party size, time, and any allergies, read back before confirming. Groups above six go to a person.
seed_garage_rule2: Parts suppliers go to the assistant
seed_garage_prompt: You answer the phone for Wagner & Partner. Take the registration and what the car is doing, then offer a service slot from the catalogue. Never estimate a repair cost over the phone.
seed_property_rule2: New enquiries go to the assistant
seed_property_prompt: You answer the phone for Wagner & Partner. Book viewings and valuations from the catalogue, and take the listing reference where there is one. Never discuss price negotiations.
seed_salon_prompt: You answer the phone for Wagner & Partner. Book from the catalogue, ask which stylist the caller wants, and read back the time and the deposit rule before confirming.
seed_office_rule1: Existing clients reach their account manager
seed_office_rule2: New enquiries go to the assistant
seed_office_prompt: You answer the phone for Wagner & Partner. Take the company name and what the call is about, then offer an intro call from the catalogue. Existing clients go to their account manager.
model_llama_31_8b_body: Handles appointments, opening hours and questions from your sources. Recommended for this machine.
model_qwen_25_14b_body: Better German, and better at callers who change their mind halfway through a sentence.
model_llama_33_70b_body: Noticeably better judgement. Needs 32 GB of memory and a graphics card to answer in time.
provider_anthropic_cost: About €0.04 per call at business length. Usage shows the real figure after a week.
model_claude_haiku_4_5_body: Enough for appointments, hours and questions from your sources. The right default for a phone line.
model_claude_sonnet_4_5_body: Better with callers who ramble or change their mind mid-sentence. The pause is audible.
model_claude_opus_4_1_body: More than a reception line needs, and long enough that callers talk over it.
provider_openai_cost: About €0.03 per call at business length.
model_gpt_41_mini_body: The cheap fast one. Handles a reception script without trouble.
model_gpt_41_body: Stronger German and better at following a long instruction block.
model_gpt_4o_body: Older but well understood, and priced lower than 4.1.
provider_mistral_cost: About €0.02 per call. EU-hosted, which shortens the data-protection conversation.
model_mistral_small_latest_body: Cheapest of the cloud options, and hosted inside the EU.
model_mistral_large_latest_body: Noticeably better German than the small one.
provider_groq_cost: About €0.01 per call — the cheapest cloud option here.
model_llama_33_70b_versatile_body: Open weights on very fast hardware. The quickest answer of anything on this screen.
model_llama_31_8b_instant_body: Faster still, but it loses track of a long instruction block.
provider_custom_cost: Whatever that endpoint charges. Tel-Agent cannot estimate it.
model_type_the_model_name_body: Ollama on another machine, vLLM, LM Studio, OpenRouter — anything that speaks the OpenAI chat format.
voice_thorsten_desc: Neutral German, instant to start speaking
side_blurb: Installing onto this machine. Nothing is sent anywhere — no account, no licence key, no phone-home.
side_config_before: Everything you set here lands in
side_config_after: . You can edit that file by hand later and skip this screen entirely.
lang_title: Which language do you work in?
lang_blurb: This is the language of the whole system: every screen, the date format, and everything Tel-Agent writes for you — greetings, emails, exports, notes. It is not the voice your callers hear — that comes later, and one installation can answer in several languages.
lang_nomatch: Nothing matches “{query}”. Search the native name or the English one — this list sets the system language, not the voices your callers hear.
lang_rtl_note: The whole system flips to right-to-left. Phone numbers, SIP hosts and log output stay left-to-right — they are always read that way.
lang_default_note: Everything Tel-Agent writes for you starts in this language: greetings, catalogue entries, notification emails. Callers can still be answered in another one.
mode_title: How much do you want to decide?
mode_blurb: Both paths end at the same place. Quick picks sensible defaults you can change afterwards; custom asks you for the database, hostname and ports up front.
mode_quick_body: For one business on one machine. Picks a file-based database, a self-signed certificate and the default ports, then gets out of the way.
mode_custom_body: For an existing server: your own Postgres, a real hostname behind your reverse proxy, and ports you choose. Nothing here is irreversible except the database.
chan_blurb: Tick what you intend to use and the right apps are downloaded now. This does not connect anything — accounts, tokens and SIP credentials come after the install, one channel at a time.
chan_none_title: Nothing ticked — nobody will be able to reach it
chan_none_body: You can install with none and add channels later from the Apps page, but the agent will sit there with no way in.
chan_note: Each channel is a small container. Adding one afterwards is a single click from the Apps page, so tick only what you are fairly sure about.
model_blurb: This is the AI that understands what a caller wants and decides what to say back. Where it runs decides whether what your customers say ever leaves the building — a legal question as much as a technical one.
place_hosted_body: Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral and the like. Answers in a few hundred milliseconds, handles awkward sentences best, and needs nothing from this machine. Every caller’s words are sent to the provider you choose.
place_local_body: Open-weight AI running beside the assistant. No account and no agreement with anyone, but slower without a graphics card.
place_mixed: On this machine, with the cloud as backup
place_mixed_body: Local by default. If it stops responding mid-call the cloud finishes the conversation instead of the line going dead.
which_models_note: On a phone call the delay before it starts speaking matters more than the depth of the answer. Pick the fast one unless you have a reason.
leave_title: Customer speech will leave your network
leave_body: Every sentence a caller says is sent to this provider to be answered. For an Austrian business that needs a data-processing agreement with them, and it belongs in what you tell customers. Speech-to-text and the voice stay on this machine either way — only the reasoning moves.
mixed_note: The local model answers every call. If it stops responding — a crash, or an update gone wrong — the hosted one takes over so the line never goes dead, and the switch is written to the call record so you know which one spoke. Set a monthly cap in Usage; a fallback nobody notices is a bill nobody expected.
voice_title: How the AI hears and speaks
voice_blurb: Two separate services: one turns the caller’s speech into text, the other turns the AI’s reply into a voice. Both add their delay to every single turn, so on a phone call their speed matters more than their quality.
stt_group: Speech to text — how it hears
stt_group_note: Runs on every sentence the caller says. A slow one makes the agent seem to hesitate.
tts_group: Text to speech — how it sounds
tts_group_note: Runs on every sentence the agent says. Natural voices cost money and start speaking later.
pair_same: Both sides are {provider} — one API key, one bill, one company to hold to an agreement.
pair_two: You are using two different companies. That means two keys, two bills and two data-processing agreements — {first} and {second} both do the other half if you would rather not.
all_local_title: Nothing here leaves your network, and nothing costs per call
all_local_body: Everything runs on hardware you control, so the only thing a call costs is the telephone minute itself — and there is no data-processing agreement to sign with anyone.
everything_leaves_title: Every part of the conversation now leaves your network
some_audio_title: Some audio will leave your network
offsite_body: Roughly {ms} ms before the agent starts speaking, and about {cost} per call on top of the minute. For a business each cloud service needs its own data-processing agreement, and customers should be told.
check_title_hosted: This machine has everything it needs
check_blurb_hosted: With the reasoning in the cloud there is very little left for this machine to do. Checked against what you picked, not against the largest thing you might have picked.
check_blurb_can: Checked against the model you chose. Nothing is written yet, so you can still go back and change it.
check_blurb_cannot: Checked against the model you chose. You can still install, but expect the caller to hear a long pause before every answer — go back and pick a smaller one.
chk_runtime_detail: Docker 27.1 — the agent, the model and the database each run in their own container.
chk_disk_none: Nothing to download — everything you picked runs somewhere else. Only call recordings and transcripts are stored here.
chk_disk_download: Downloading {size} GB of models, plus room for recordings and transcripts.
chk_mem_hosted: Plenty — the reasoning happens at your provider, so this machine only moves audio around.
chk_mem_ok: {model} needs about {gb} GB and leaves room for the database and the voice.
chk_mem_fail: {model} needs about {gb} GB. It will load, then swap to disk and answer several seconds late.
chk_gfx_hosted: Not needed. Speech-to-text runs fast enough on the processor alone.
chk_gfx_cpu: No GPU found, so the model runs on the processor. Roughly a second before it starts speaking — acceptable, but a card would halve it.
chk_ports_detail: Web interface, SIP signalling and the media range are all free.
chk_smtp_detail: Port 587 is blocked, so notification emails cannot be sent yet. Everything else works — set this up later in Settings.
smaller_title: Pick a smaller model, or a bigger machine
smaller_body: On 16 GB with no graphics card this model answers a caller about four seconds late — long enough that they say “hello?” again and talk over it. llama-3.1-8b answers in under a second and handles appointments, opening hours and questions from your sources perfectly well.
hosted_note_title: Memory and graphics do not matter for your setup
hosted_note_body: You picked a cloud model, so this machine never loads one. All it does locally is turn speech into text and text into speech, which any modern processor manages in real time. What matters instead is your internet connection — a dropout mid-call means the caller hears silence.
db_title: Where calls and transcripts are stored
db_blurb: Two options, because a third would mean a third thing to test against every release and it would buy you nothing. MySQL and MariaDB are not supported on purpose — neither has vector search worth using, and the agent needs it to answer from your own documents.
db_file_body: SQLite with full-text and vector search built in. No database to install, no separate backup — copying one file copies everything. Comfortable past two hundred calls a day, which is more than a single business makes.
db_pg_body: Worth the extra moving part for two reasons only: a knowledge library too large for local vector search, or two Tel-Agent instances reading the same data. Brings replication and point-in-time restore with it.
db_footer_note: Nothing is written until this succeeds.
host_blurb: The hostname goes into the desk-phone provisioning code and into every link in a notification email, so a wrong value here breaks both quietly.
f_hostname_help: What phones and browsers use to reach this machine.
f_tls_help: Let’s Encrypt needs a public name; a self-signed certificate makes desk phones refuse to register.
f_sip_help: TLS on 5061 is what Austrian providers expect.
f_rtp_help: Must be open on the firewall or callers hear silence in one direction.
f_proxy_help: Trust forwarded headers from your proxy only.
host_note: SIP needs a stable address. On a home connection with a changing IP the line will drop every time the router reconnects — a static IP or a dynamic-DNS name is not optional for a business phone.
admin_blurb: Local to this machine. There is no password reset by email until you set up SMTP, so write this one down.
admin_note: Fourteen characters, one word you will remember. Length beats symbols — and there is no email reset until SMTP works.
inst_blurb_none: Nothing to download — every model you picked runs at a provider. This takes a few seconds.
inst_blurb: {what} is the slow part: {size} GB in total, and it only happens once.
task_db: Created the database and its tables
task_speech_detail: 1.2 GB of 1.8 GB · about 2 minutes left
inst_close_before: You can close this tab. The install carries on and the log is at
line_blurb: Tel-Agent is installed and running. This is the part that needs your telephone provider — the credentials are stored encrypted on this machine and are sent nowhere else.
line_footer_note: Most providers send these four values in one email. Paste the host and username and Tel-Agent guesses the rest.
trade_title: What kind of work is this line for?
trade_blurb: Tel-Agent knows nothing about any trade. Pick the closest one and it writes a starting catalogue, a few routing rules and the assistant’s first instructions — as ordinary data you can edit or delete.
seed_counts: {services} services · {fields} contact fields · {rules} routing rules · {qa} written answers
trade_empty_body: Nothing is created. The catalogue, the routing rules and the assistant’s answers all start empty, and you write them yourself on the Catalogue screen.
trade_footer: All of it is ordinary data on your own machine. Nothing is locked to a trade — rename it, delete it, or start again with a different one.
greet_blurb: The greeting is filled in from your business name, and the voice comes from the engine you chose during the install. Both are easy to change later.
greet_text: {business}, good morning. This call is recorded. How can I help you?
greet_note: Callers are told the call is recorded because you switched recording on. Remove that sentence and recording switches off too.
voice_local_note: Piper on this machine — no account, nothing leaves your network.
voice_engine_note: From the engine you picked during the install.
book_body: Connect your calendar now or later. Until you do, the assistant takes messages instead of booking.
done_title: Everything is set up. Ring your own number.
done_blurb: The last step is the only one that proves it works: call the line and talk to the assistant the way a customer would. The call appears in your list, transcribed, straight away.
done_call_note: Your phone rings in a few seconds. Hang up when you are done — nothing else is waiting on you.
fr_blurb: One account, on this machine. There is no cloud login, and nothing you type here leaves the building.
fr_username_help: What you will sign in with. Local to this installation.
fr_password_help: At least twelve characters. A sentence you can remember beats a short string you cannot — and until a mail server is configured, nobody can reset it for you.
fr_workspace_help: The workspace everything belongs to. It can be renamed later.
fr_email_help: Optional. Where a reset code would go once a mail server is configured.
fr_short: That password is too short. Twelve characters at least.
fr_taken: This installation was set up while you were on this page. Sign in instead.
fr_offline: The server did not answer. It may not be running yet.
fr_failed: Something went wrong setting up. Nothing was created, so you can try again.
fr_done_body: The account, the workspace and the web chat channel exist. Two things are worth doing before anybody writes in.
fr_next_model: Connect a model, so the agent can answer
fr_next_widget: Switch the web chat on, and put it on your site
fr_already_title: This installation is already set up
fr_already_body: An account exists on this machine, so first run is over. Sign in with it.
